description: SYRAX represents the spirit of exploration, innovation, and discovery. Inspired by NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars, our team focuses on the forgotten technology and untold stories left behind during humanity's greatest space missions. We believe that even abandoned objects carry valuable history, knowledge, and possibilities for the future. Just as space exploration never truly ends,  stands for curiosity, creativity, and the determination to rediscover what others have left
summary:
Here's a summary of about 130 words that you can paste in:

 We  story presentation on NASA's Constellation Program (2005 to 2010), the abandoned effort to return humans to the Moon. It explains what the program was, gives a timeline from the 2004 Vision for Space Exploration to its 2010 cancellation, and describes its four main hardware elements: Orion, Ares I, Ares V and Altair. It also covers what the program achieved, including the Ares I-X test flight and the Orion Pad Abort-1 test, and why it failed: a budget gap, schedule delays and technical problems such as Ares I vibration.      The project addresses the challenge by examining why an ambitious exploration plan collapsed and what survived it. Orion and Shuttle-derived hardware live on in the Artemis program and the Space Launch System. This matters because it shows that ambitious space programs need stable funding and realistic schedules, lessons that still apply to today's Moon and Mars plans.

The deck is a research presentation rather than something you built, so I wrote "developed" to mean the presentation second paragraph.
details: We developed a seven-slide presentation on NASA's Constellation Program (2005 to 2010), the abandoned plan to return humans to the Moon. It covers the program's goals, timeline, hardware (Orion, Ares I, Ares V and Altair), achievements, and why it was cancelled: budget, delays and technical risk. It matters because it shows that ambitious space programs need stable funding and realistic schedules.
